in_arabic.name: لُجَيْن
in_arabic.long_meaning: اللُجَيْنُ الماءُ المذكى الذي يُستَخدَم في التَعَميقِ والغَسيلِ، ويُمكن أن يُستَعْمَلُ لِلقَولِ عَنِ الماءِ المذكى، وَهوَ مِنَ الأَسْماءِ الثِقافِيَّةِ التِي تُشيرُ إلى الحِلمِ والإِخلاصِ، وَيَقولُ الْعَرَبُ: لُجَيَنَ الماءَ لِأَنَّهُ يَضِيءُ الماءَ المذكى، وَقَد ذُكِرَ في الْقُرْآنِ الْکَرِيمِ في سُورَةِ الأِنفِطَالِ، وَيُمكن أن يُستَعْمَلَ لِلقَولِ عَنِ الإِخلاصِ والصِدقِ

in_urdu.name: لُجَیں

data.cultural_impact: The name Lujayn carries a rich cultural heritage rooted in the Arabic language and the unique musical rhythm of the name. The name resonates with the enchantment of the night and the exquisiteness of the jasmine flower, which is deeply cherished in Islamic culture. data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Lujayn lies in its association with the night and the jasmine flower. In Islamic tradition, the night is considered a time of reflection, restoration, and renewal. The verse in the Quran, "We send down from the cloud pouring water and We produce through it gardens and harvest for them: lo and behold, in this is Indeed a Sign" (Quran 30:50), highlights the important role of water and the renewal it brings during the night. Jasmine, with its sweet aroma, is also considered to have spiritual significance in various Islamic traditions, symbolizing purity and beauty. The name Lujayn thus represents the combination of these spiritual iterations, embodying the essence of renewal, restoration and beauty in the night.
